constructs.name: Generic verb to situated verb
constructs.definition: One side is dominated by semantically light, all-purpose words that would complete almost any sentence of that shape, while the other is dominated by words whose meaning depends on the particular situation being described.
constructs.nearest: It is nearest to the collapse-to-a-hedge construct, since both describe one side declining to name a determinate act, but here the non-committal side is a broad pool of many interchangeable light verbs whereas there the mass concentrates on a single word.

constructs.name: Blunt word, formal counterpart
constructs.definition: Both sides name substantially the same act, and the difference is one of register alone: colloquial and abrupt vocabulary on one side, its institutional or professional synonym on the other.
constructs.nearest: It is nearest to the withdrawal-to-redress construct, but there the act itself changes (one side ends the involvement, the other continues it), whereas here the act is constant and only its lexical dress moves; the clearest evidence that these are two is that the formal exit word sits on the elevated side in these two descriptions and on the drastic side in rb78dfc1.

constructs.name: Withdrawal to redress
constructs.definition: One side's words end or abandon the involvement, or capitulate within it, while the other side's words continue it by contesting, appealing, or proceeding through an available channel.
constructs.nearest: It is nearest to the blunt-word construct, and is distinguished by the fact that the two sides here denote different courses of action rather than two names for one, so a description can place formal and informal exit words together on the same side.

constructs.name: Spread collapses to hedge
constructs.definition: A wide set of distinct, decisive action words on one side gives way on the other to near-total concentration on a single word that completes a hedging idiom rather than naming an act.
constructs.nearest: It is nearest to the non-naming stand-in construct, and differs in that its claim is about the shape of the whole distribution narrowing, not only about which word occupies the top of it.

constructs.name: Non-naming stand-in
constructs.definition: The high-probability slot on one side is taken by a word that names no action at all and merely intensifies or frames an act left unspecified, where the other side goes directly to a verb.
constructs.nearest: It is nearest to the collapse-to-a-hedge construct, but it makes no claim that the surrounding spread narrows, and its stand-in is a bare intensifier rather than one term of a fixed idiom.

unassigned.description: Every description made a claim specific enough to place, though r43c8113 was the marginal case: its wording is internally confused about which side the drops belong to, and it was assigned to the collapse construct on the strength of its side assignments, which are structurally identical to ra4e5703's.

result.topic_audit: Every one of the fourteen descriptions is drawn from what looks like a single subject matter, a person disciplined at work deciding whether to leave, so all five constructs share a topic and no construct could have been produced by topic sorting, because topic is constant across the whole set and therefore does no discriminating work. The check that matters here is the opposite one, whether the shared subject has made me split too finely or merge too coarsely, and the discriminating evidence is that descriptions covering the same vocabulary land in different constructs: rd4ca354 puts quit, leave and resign on its situated side while rb78dfc1 puts the same three on its drastic-exit side, so the two cannot be one construct despite quoting nearly the same words. The boundary I am least sure of is between the blunt-word construct and the withdrawal-to-redress construct, since r22d0464 and r31bfd4e both oppose informal quitting to formal procedural vocabulary and could be read as register in one case and as a change of act in the other; I split them on whether the formal side still denotes leaving, which is a real distinction but a thin one on these two entries. I am also unsure whether ra9d21c2 should stand alone rather than join the collapse construct, and whether r5dcda9f's emphasis on idiomatic completions pulls it toward the collapse construct rather than the generic-to-situated one.
result.notes: One structural regularity supports the partition and is worth recording: within each construct the direction is consistent, with A always the generic side in the first construct, always the blunt side in the second, always the exit side in the third, and always the broad-spread side in the fourth. Across constructs the direction is not shared, which is the strongest single piece of evidence that the generic-to-situated construct and the withdrawal-to-redress construct name different differences rather than one difference described twice, since the words classed as situated in the first are precisely the words classed as withdrawal in the third. Two descriptions in the fourth construct name literally the same B-side word, which raises the possibility that they are two readings of one pair rather than two independent instances of a kind; I have kept them as one construct because the relation they name is the same either way, but a construct with only one underlying pair behind it is weaker evidence than its two members suggest.

__key__.frame_prompt: He was written up for the third time this month, so he decided to

constructs.name: Generic to situation-bound
constructs.definition: One side's words are semantically light, all-purpose items that would fit almost any sentence of that shape, while the other side's words take their meaning from the particular situation being described.
constructs.nearest: Decisive act to hedge, because that construct also contrasts contentful with contentless completions, but it runs the other way round: there the specific, contentful options sit on side A and the empty formula on side B, whereas here the situation-bound options are what side B supplies.

constructs.name: Colloquial to formal counterpart
constructs.definition: Both sides name the same underlying act, but one uses the blunt everyday term for it and the other its elevated, register-marked synonym.
constructs.nearest: Direct act to procedure, and the difference is that this construct changes only the name of the act while that one changes the act itself, substituting a mediated response for the thing named.

constructs.name: Direct act to procedure
constructs.definition: One side takes an act immediately and on one's own account, while the other routes an equivalent response through formal, written, or third-party procedure.
constructs.nearest: Withdrawal to contestation, which also replaces disengagement with a response made in place, but there the response is opposition to the party responsible, whereas here it is compliance with a sanctioned route that takes no position against anyone.

constructs.name: Withdrawal to contestation
constructs.definition: One side's option is to leave, avoid, or carry on as before, while the other's is to stay in the situation and push back against the party responsible for it.
constructs.nearest: Direct act to procedure, from which it differs in that the vocabulary introduced on the second side is adversarial and interpersonal rather than procedural, so that what changes is the stance toward an authority rather than the route an action takes.

constructs.name: Decisive act to hedge
constructs.definition: A broad spread of decisive, high-commitment options on one side contracts on the other onto a non-committal formula that completes the sentence without naming any act.
constructs.nearest: Deferral by modifier, which likewise ends in a completion that names no act, but there the act is still coming and merely postponed, whereas here the hedging formula takes the act's place outright.

constructs.name: Deferral by modifier
constructs.definition: One side supplies the content word that names the act, while the other's most prominent item is a contentless modifier that delays the act rather than replacing or naming it.
constructs.nearest: Decisive act to hedge, which it is not because the modifier here intensifies and postpones a verb that still arrives, rather than substituting a different and weaker completion for it.

unassigned.description: Every description named a difference specific enough to place, so nothing was set aside as too vague; the closest call was r43c8113, whose prose contradicts itself about which side the drops occur on, but its two word lists make its shape unambiguous and identical to ra4e5703's.

result.topic_audit: All six constructs share a subject matter, because all fourteen descriptions do: every one of them is drawn from what looks like a single scenario, a person disciplined at work deciding whether to quit, and the recurring vocabulary of quit, resign, file, and write-up runs through descriptions I have placed in six different constructs. That means the usual guard is satisfied only trivially here, and it also means I cannot use topical divergence as evidence that any group is a construct, since there is no topical divergence anywhere in the set. The risk in this set runs the opposite way from the one the instructions warn about: not that I have grouped by topic, but that I have sliced one topic into distinctions finer than the underlying difference. Generic to situation-bound is the group I am most confident in, because its five members agree on an axis that is explicitly about the relation between a word and any sentence at all, and three of them say so in the abstract before quoting anything. Decisive act to hedge is next most secure, because both members exhibit a many-to-one collapse onto the same single completion and both make the narrowing itself, rather than the content of the words, the thing described. The three I am unsure about are Colloquial to formal counterpart, Direct act to procedure, and Withdrawal to contestation, which sit adjacent to one another and could be argued to be one construct about the replacement of impulsive exit by a measured in-place response; I keep them apart because what changes differs in each, being the name of the act, the route of the act, and the stance toward an authority respectively, but a reader who called them one would not be making a topic error. I am also unsure whether rb78dfc1 belongs in Direct act to procedure or in Decisive act to hedge, since its stated axis is abrupt against measured as much as it is direct against procedural.
result.notes: One structural fact runs across the whole set and is worth recording because no single description states it: the polarity is consistent, in that side A always holds the blunter, more generic, or more decisive vocabulary and side B always holds the more specific, more formal, more procedural, or more hedged vocabulary, with no description reversing it. That consistency is what let me treat descriptions whose wording seemed opposed, such as r41083a9 and rd4ca354, as naming one difference rather than two. The prompt says these descriptions were written about many different sentences on many different subjects, and on the evidence in front of me that is not the case, since all fourteen quote the same disciplinary-workplace vocabulary and four of them mention being written up explicitly; if that framing is right then something upstream has selected a single-topic sample, and if it is wrong then the warning about topic-grouping has no purchase on this set. r43c8113 says the largest drops occur under A and then infers that the drastic resolutions lose rank under B, which cannot both be true; I read it by its word lists, which place the drastic verbs on A and the single word step on B, matching ra4e5703 exactly.

__key__.frame_prompt: He was written up for the third time this month, so he decided to

constructs.name: Light verb, bound verb
constructs.definition: One side favors semantically light, all-purpose words that would fit almost any sentence of that shape, while the other favors words whose meaning is tied to the particular situation being described.
constructs.nearest: Closest to "Blunt to formal register", but that construct has both sides naming the same act in two styles, whereas here one side's words do not engage the situation at all and could be swapped into another sentence without loss.

constructs.name: Blunt to formal register
constructs.definition: Both sides name substantially the same act, but one side reaches for the blunt colloquial word and the other for its formal, institutionally sanctioned counterpart.
constructs.nearest: Closest to "Exit versus contestation", which also puts procedural vocabulary on one side; the difference is that here the act is unchanged and only its register moves, while there the act itself changes from ending the situation to staying inside it.

constructs.name: Exit versus contestation
constructs.definition: One side favors ending, withdrawing from, or giving in to the situation, while the other favors remaining inside it and pushing back, whether by formal procedure or by direct confrontation.
constructs.nearest: Closest to "Blunt to formal register", because the pushing-back side often arrives in procedural clothing; it is not that construct because the two sides here are not two names for one act, and one member's contesting side is openly non-formal (fight, confront, tell).

constructs.name: Drastic loses most
constructs.definition: The movement between the two sides is selective by consequentiality: the most decisive, high-commitment options are precisely the ones that lose the most ground, and what replaces them is a milder option that still names an action.
constructs.nearest: Closest to "Action replaced by non-action"; it differs because something that is still an act survives on the receiving side (retire, appeal, seek, ask), so the description is about which acts fall rather than about an act being displaced by a word that names none.

constructs.name: Action replaced by non-action
constructs.definition: The leading option on one side names an act directly, while the leading option on the other side names no act at all, being an intensifier or a hedging idiom that frames or defers rather than resolves.
constructs.nearest: Closest to "Drastic loses most", from which it is separated by what arrives rather than by what departs: here the replacement carries no action content of its own, so no alternative course is being proposed.

unassigned.description: Every description states a kind of difference specific enough to place, so nothing is left over; the two I came closest to setting aside were r43c8113, which qualifies itself with an exception ('quit' does not follow the pattern), and r6b58c8f, whose contesting side oddly includes the exit word 'quit' alongside fight and file, but in both cases the named relation is clear enough to defend.

result.topic_audit: Topic could not have done the sorting here even if I had let it: essentially all fourteen descriptions quote the same scenario vocabulary (quit, resign, leave, being written up, filing something), so subject matter is close to constant across the whole set and cannot separate any group from any other. "Light verb, bound verb" is the safest on this count: its five members share the abstract contrast but not their evidence, since one member's specific side is job-departure words, another's is evasion and enlistment, another's is idiomatic coping (clean up, lay low, plead), and another's generic side is everyday unrelated verbs (see, visit, play, buy) rather than light verbs at all. "Blunt to formal register" is the one I am least sure of, because both members almost certainly come from the same sentence and both rest on the same quit/resign pair; I keep it because the relation they name, one act in two registers, is stated by nothing else in the set, and because r22d0464, which shares that flavor of vocabulary, is placed elsewhere on grounds of kind. "Exit versus contestation" spans at least two different sentences, its contesting sides being file/write/take, fight/file, and confront/fight/talk/tell, so it is not held together by shared wording. "Drastic loses most" deliberately crosses sentences: r43c8113's receiving side is the single word 'step' while rb78dfc1's is retire/appeal/seek/stay, and the grouping rests on the selectivity claim rather than on evidence they share. The matching risk sits in "Action replaced by non-action", whose two members are what a skeptic should attack first, since ra4e5703 shares the 'step' item with r43c8113, which I put in a different construct; I have therefore split one apparent item across two constructs and merged two apparent items into one, which is the right way round if the kinds are real and is exactly where to look if they are not.
result.notes: Two structural observations. First, direction is uniform: in all fourteen, side A carries the blunter, more specific, more drastic, more directly action-naming material and side B the milder, more procedural, more generic or more deferring material. That consistency is why the five constructs read as five angles on one underlying shift rather than five unrelated axes, and someone who wanted to collapse the answer to two constructs (specificity and commitment) would have a case; I kept five because the descriptions themselves distinguish register from specificity from act-substitution, and collapsing would discard distinctions their authors made explicitly. Second, the answer turns on two decisions. r22d0464 was moved out of the register construct despite its formal-procedural vocabulary, because its two sides are two different acts (giving in versus filing something) rather than two names for one act. And r43c8113 was separated from ra4e5703 despite both resolving onto the single word 'step', because r43c8113 claims that the most consequential words lose the most rank while ra4e5703 claims that a broad spread narrows onto a word naming no act. If either decision is wrong, the affected constructs merge rather than dissolve.

constructs.name: Transgressive to permitted
constructs.definition: One side concentrates on explicit or taboo vocabulary and the other side supplies a socially permitted alternative that fills the same slot for the same action, so that the difference between the sides is one of propriety rather than of what is being done.
constructs.nearest: It is closest to the same-referent register swap, and it is not that one because there the two sides go on naming the very same thing under a different label, whereas here the permitted side names a different thing entirely, which is what allows the description to stay inoffensive.

constructs.name: Range narrowing
constructs.definition: One side spreads its mass across many items drawn from a wide field while the other confines almost all of its mass to a small cluster or a handful of items, so the named difference is how broadly the preference is distributed rather than which items are preferred.
constructs.nearest: It is closest to the transgressive-to-permitted construct, and two of its three members do also remark on explicitness, but the relation each of them puts forward as the finding is a change in the width of the distribution, which would still hold if both sides were drawn from the same propriety register.

constructs.name: Subtype to superordinate
constructs.definition: Both sides pick out the same broad domain, but one side prefers the specific named subtype and the other prefers the general category term that would cover it, a move up or down the ladder of taxonomic level with no change of field.
constructs.nearest: It is closest to range narrowing, and it is not that one because a taxonomic ascent can be stated on a single pair of words with no reference to how many items each side holds, while range narrowing is a claim about the spread of the whole set.

constructs.name: Same-referent register swap
constructs.definition: Both sides denote one and the same thing and differ only in which synonym from a shared pool is favored, so the change is in the tone or formality of the naming rather than in what is named.
constructs.nearest: It is closest to transgressive-to-permitted, and it is not that one because no side is made acceptable by the swap; the two describers explicitly note that both sides remain within the same explicit vocabulary and merely reach for different members of it.

constructs.name: Recipient-class shift
constructs.definition: The entity occupying the receiving end of the action changes class between the two sides, from one kind of being or relation to another, with neither side more or less permissible than the other.
constructs.nearest: It is closest to transgressive-to-permitted, whose permitted side often also installs a new recipient, and it is not that one because here both recipients are equally sayable and the description offers no propriety axis at all, only a reclassification of who or what is on the other end.

constructs.name: Modifier entrainment
constructs.definition: The difference appears not in the referring terms themselves but in the dependent words that would attach to them, which sort to whichever side carries the head they belong with, so the construct names a grammatical co-selection rather than a substitution.
constructs.nearest: It is closest to transgressive-to-permitted, since the two pools of modifiers land on the two sides that the propriety split had already created, and it is not that one because the modifiers themselves carry no charge; they follow their heads, and the finding is the following, not the split.

constructs.name: Possessive frame shift
constructs.definition: The two sides prefer different grammatical forms of a term for the same entity, one form projecting a further element after it and the other standing alone, so the change is in the construction the word opens rather than in the word's reference or tone.
constructs.nearest: It is closest to the same-referent register swap, and it is not that one because the possessive and the bare form do not pick out the same thing: the possessive points past the entity to something belonging to it, which changes what is finally being talked about.

unassigned.description: Every description named a relation definite enough to place, so nothing is left over; the two I came closest to setting aside were r97dba1f and rea44798, which each state two relations at once, but both put a claim about distributional width in the foreground and so could be placed on that rather than parked.

result.topic_audit: All seven constructs share a subject matter, and they share the same one: every description in this batch concerns touching or stroking a body, so the usual test of asking whether a group is held together by its topic cannot separate anything here, since a topical grouping would return all twenty-one ids as a single pile. The audit therefore has to ask a different question, namely whether each group is held together by the relation it names once the shared vocabulary is discounted. Transgressive-to-permitted is the group most at risk of being merely a topic, since its members quote heavily overlapping word lists; I am confident it is a construct because the direction reverses in r7e14d30, which puts the explicit pool on the opposite side, and a topical grouping would not survive that inversion, and because the permitted material varies across body parts, pets, relatives, romantic partners and an inanimate object while the propriety axis is what every member actually asserts. Range narrowing draws on the same anatomical vocabulary as that group, which is exactly why I am least sure of it: r97dba1f and rea44798 both mention explicitness alongside width, and a reader who took explicitness as primary would move both into the first construct and leave rc203b05 nearly alone. Subtype-to-superordinate spans animals and facial hair, which is the clearest case of a construct cutting across subject matter within this batch. Same-referent register swap, recipient-class shift, modifier entrainment and possessive frame shift are each distinguishable by a formal property, respectively the constancy of reference, the reclassification of the patient, grammatical dependency and syntactic projection, none of which depends on what the sentence is about. The placements I am unsure of are the two double-coded ids just named, and r19adf27, r257f2ac and rd6b0e81, all of which install a new recipient alongside the propriety swap and could be read as belonging with recipient-class shift instead.
result.notes: The batch is not the mixed-subject set the instructions anticipate: all twenty-one descriptions appear to come from one sentence frame, so the warning against grouping by topic loses its diagnostic force and the constructs had to be cut on relational form alone. That makes the largest construct the weakest guarantee, because ten descriptions using one vocabulary will look unified whether or not they name one kind of difference. Three descriptions state two relations at once and their assignment rests on which relation each foregrounds, which is a reading of the describer's emphasis rather than a measurement; a different reader could redistribute r97dba1f, rea44798, r19adf27, r257f2ac and rd6b0e81 without contradicting anything on the page. The two single-member constructs are kept because each names something no other description names, a dependent word following its head and a possessive projecting a further noun, and folding either into a neighbor would assert a sameness the descriptions do not support.

constructs.name: Transgressive to permitted substitution
constructs.definition: One side supplies items that a norm treats as unsayable while the other supplies a licit item that could occupy the very same slot in the same construction, so the difference is between naming the forbidden thing and naming an allowed stand-in for it.
constructs.nearest: Its nearest neighbour is Synonym pool reallocation, and it is not that construct because there both sides still name the same prohibited thing and only the choice of word moves, whereas here one side declines to name it at all and offers a different, permitted referent in its place.

constructs.name: Synonym pool reallocation
constructs.definition: Both sides name the same referent and draw from the same pool of near-synonyms for it, differing only in which members of that pool they prefer.
constructs.nearest: Its nearest neighbour is Transgressive to permitted substitution, and it is not that construct because nothing is being avoided or replaced: the referent is constant across both sides and only register or lexical habit shifts, so no substitute object is ever supplied.

constructs.name: Broad field, narrow cluster
constructs.definition: One side's items range across a whole domain while the other's are confined to a small subregion of that domain or to a handful of items, with neither side treated as unsayable.
constructs.nearest: Its nearest neighbour is Instance to category label, and it is not that construct because both sides here sit at the same level of generality and what changes is how much of the field is covered and how concentrated the weight is, not whether members or their superordinate term are the ones being named.

constructs.name: Instance to category label
constructs.definition: One side names particular members of a class while the other names the class itself, with the extension held roughly constant so that the same things are being referred to at a different level of naming.
constructs.nearest: Its nearest neighbour is Broad field, narrow cluster, and it is not that construct because the covered domain neither widens nor shrinks; the move is up a taxonomic level rather than out across or into a field.

constructs.name: Reassigned licit object
constructs.definition: The entity occupying one and the same slot changes from one permitted kind to another along a dimension such as relation, kinship, or animacy, with neither pole under any prohibition.
constructs.nearest: Its nearest neighbour is Transgressive to permitted substitution, and it is not that construct because nothing on either side is being avoided, so the change is a reassignment among equally sayable options rather than an evasion of one of them.

constructs.name: Modifiers follow heads
constructs.definition: The difference falls on grammatical dependents rather than on the items they attach to, with the modifiers sorting to the same side as the heads they would qualify.
constructs.nearest: Its nearest neighbour is Transgressive to permitted substitution, and it is not that construct because it does not describe one item standing in for another at all but a covariation in which a class of words drags its grammatical satellites along with it.

constructs.name: Construction over content
constructs.definition: The two sides prefer different grammatical forms or constructions built on what is otherwise the same term, so the contrast is between forms rather than between things named.
constructs.nearest: Its nearest neighbour is Reassigned licit object, and it is not that construct because the entity referred to does not change; one side selects a form that projects a further dependent noun while the other selects a bare, less marked form of the same relation.

unassigned.description: Every description named a relation specific enough to place, so nothing is left over; the two I came closest to setting aside were r97dba1f and rea44798, which each name two relations at once, but in both cases one of the two is stated as the governing contrast and that was enough to assign them rather than abandon them.

result.topic_audit: Almost every description in this batch is drawn from the same subject matter -- somebody touching a body -- so topic is very nearly constant across all twenty-one and cannot by itself be what any of my groups is tracking; the risk here is the inverse of the usual one, namely that a real construct will look like a topic simply because there is only one topic available. Transgressive to permitted substitution is the group where that risk bites hardest, because all eleven members quote explicit sexual vocabulary and someone could fairly say I have merely collected the descriptions that mention genitals; what persuades me it is a construct is that four other descriptions quote exactly the same vocabulary and are not in it (r4e43116 and rbde40e6 quote the same words but hold the referent constant, r2a2661b quotes only the modifiers attached to those words, r97dba1f quotes them but names concentration as the relation), so membership is decided by the relation and not by the lexicon. Broad field, narrow cluster shares the body-part vocabulary among its three members, but two of them run in opposite directions (rc203b05 goes broad-to-narrow and r03e1490 narrow-to-broad) and one of them, r97dba1f, is about where the weight piles up rather than which region is covered, so the shared subject is doing no work in holding them together. Instance to category label stands alone and is about animals, which is also r17d1e06's subject matter and yet the two are in different constructs, which is the cleanest evidence in this batch that I am not sorting by topic. Reassigned licit object is the group I am least sure of: both members involve relational nouns for people, and I am grouping them on the claim that a shift from animal to spouse and a shift from kin to romantic partner are the same kind of move among equally permitted objects, which is defensible but would be much easier to test against a batch drawn from other sentences. Synonym pool reallocation is the second one I flag, since both its members concern the same synonym set and I have nothing outside that set to show the construct generalizes. Modifiers follow heads and Construction over content each have one member and no topic to share.
result.notes: The A and B labels are not a stable condition assignment across these raters: eight descriptions put the explicit vocabulary on A while r7e14d30, rd6b0e81 and r97dba1f put it on B, so polarity carries no information here and every construct above is written direction-neutrally, naming the kind of change rather than which side changed. Three descriptions name two relations at once and their placement is the judgment call I would most expect a second reader to contest. rea44798 opens with breadth (a broad range of parts against a confined beard cluster) and closes with sexual against non-sexual, and I put it with the substitution construct because its closing clause makes the sexual reading the payoff; r97dba1f has the same double shape and I put it with breadth because its sentence is built on spread against concentration; r7bd919f mentions intensity modifiers riding along with the genital nouns, which is exactly what r2a2661b isolates, but its headline relation is explicit against everyday so it stays with the substitution construct. If those three were reassigned, the substitution construct would lose two members and the breadth construct would gain one, which is the main axis of instability in this answer. The larger caveat is that with a single sentence behind the whole batch I cannot test any construct against a genuinely different subject matter, which is what keeps my confidence at medium rather than high.

constructs.definition: One side's high-ranking items are the vocabulary a norm marks as forbidden or intimate, and the other side's are ordinary items that could fill the very same slot, so the difference is whether the marked thing is named outright or a permitted stand-in occupies its place.
constructs.nearest: Its nearest neighbor is Lateral referent swap, which also exchanges whatever occupies the object slot, but there neither candidate is the marked one, so nothing is being defused and the swap has no direction of permission to it.

constructs.name: Wide scatter, tight cluster
constructs.definition: One side spreads its mass thinly across a wide range of co-ordinate candidates while the other collapses almost entirely onto a small tightly bound subregion of the same field, so the difference is in how concentrated the distribution is rather than in which kind of item it prefers.
constructs.nearest: Its nearest neighbor is Abstraction level shift, since both have a side that covers more ground, but abstraction covers ground with one superordinate word while this construct covers it by distributing mass over many sibling words, and a narrow cluster of specific words is narrow without being abstract.

constructs.name: Same referent, rival synonyms
constructs.definition: Both sides name the same thing throughout and differ only in which member of an interchangeable naming set they favor, so the difference is lexical selection under a constant referent rather than any change in what is being talked about.
constructs.nearest: Its nearest neighbor is Explicit versus sanitized, because both describe rival words competing for one slot, but here the referent never changes and neither side supplies a permitted substitute, so what varies is register or idiom rather than whether the thing is named at all.

constructs.name: Lateral referent swap
constructs.definition: The entity that the action applies to is exchanged for an entity of a different category but comparable ordinariness, so the difference lies in which class of thing occupies the slot and not in whether either class is permitted.
constructs.nearest: Its nearest neighbor is Explicit versus sanitized, which uses the same substitution mechanics, but that construct always has one marked and one unmarked side, whereas both sides here are equally sayable and the swap carries no asymmetry of permission.

constructs.name: Abstraction level shift
constructs.definition: One side prefers words naming particular instances while the other prefers the superordinate category word that covers them, so the difference is the taxonomic level at which the same field is named.
constructs.nearest: Its nearest neighbor is Wide scatter, tight cluster; it is not that one because the change described is in the level of the individual word rather than in how many words share the probability mass, and a set of particular names can be just as small as the category word that subsumes them.

constructs.name: Modifiers follow their head
constructs.definition: The observable difference is carried by grammatically dependent words that are pulled along by whatever the item they modify has become, so the contrast surfaces in a satellite word class rather than in the item that actually changed.
constructs.nearest: Its nearest neighbor is Explicit versus sanitized, since the modifiers ride on exactly that substitution, but the claim being made is about which grammatical category registers the shift, and the modifiers themselves are not marked or unmarked in the way the head words are.

constructs.name: Grammatical form, same word
constructs.definition: One lexical item appears on both sides in different grammatical constructions, one of which projects further material after it and the other of which stands alone, so the difference is syntactic frame rather than content.
constructs.nearest: Its nearest neighbor is Same referent, rival synonyms, because both hold the referent fixed and vary only the wording, but a possessive and a bare form are one word in two frames rather than two competing words, and the contrast here predicts what comes next in the string.

unassigned.description: Every description made a claim specific enough to place, so nothing is parked here; the two I came closest to leaving unassigned were r97dba1f and rea44798, which make two claims at once (breadth of spread and explicitness), and I assigned each by the claim its own name and opening clause leads with rather than by the words it happens to quote.

result.topic_audit: The usual test is degenerate for this batch: all twenty-one descriptions quote words that fit one and the same frame, something like a person beginning to stroke his something, so shared topic is universal here and cannot by itself distinguish a construct from a topic. What does the work instead is that the sub-topics inside that frame cut across my constructs rather than lining up with them. Genital vocabulary appears in Explicit versus sanitized, in Same referent rival synonyms, and in Modifiers follow their head; facial hair appears in Explicit versus sanitized (r096d02f, r7a8495d, rf69eb30) and again in Wide scatter tight cluster (r03e1490, rc203b05, rea44798); animals appear in four different constructs (r257f2ac and rf69eb30 as sanitized substitutes, r17d1e06 as a lateral swap, r61d8d3d as an abstraction contrast); relational nouns for people appear in Explicit versus sanitized, in Lateral referent swap, and in Grammatical form same word. Construct by construct: Explicit versus sanitized shares no single sub-topic, since its innocuous side is variously beards, hands, pets, relatives, and torsos, and I am confident it is a construct because what its members agree on is the markedness asymmetry, not the substitute. Wide scatter tight cluster does lean toward one sub-topic, the beard and chin region, in three of its four members, and this is the one I am least sure of; I keep it because r97dba1f's tight side is explicit genital words rather than facial hair, which shows the shape claim can be made with the sub-topic removed, but a fourth member from a different sentence would settle it and I do not have one. Same referent rival synonyms shares a sub-topic outright, both members being about slang for the same body part, and I hold it as a construct because the defining move, holding the referent constant while shuffling the name, is stated in both and is exactly what the largest construct never does; still, with two same-topic members it is the second one I would want challenged. Lateral referent swap shares no sub-topic, its two members involving animals and kin terms respectively. The three single-member constructs cannot share a topic with themselves, and each was kept because its claim is about a mechanism (dependent-word tracking, syntactic frame, taxonomic level) that no other description makes.
result.notes: Three things a reader should know about how I grouped. First, direction is not treated as part of construct identity. Most members of Explicit versus sanitized put the explicit vocabulary on A, but r7e14d30 and rd6b0e81 put it on B, and since the raters saw different sentences and were given no vocabulary or orientation convention, I cannot tell whether that flip is a real reversal of the underlying pair or just a difference in which list a rater called A; grouping on the axis and recording the polarity separately seemed more honest than making two constructs whose only difference might be labeling. Second, several descriptions carry two claims and I assigned each to one construct on the strength of the name its author gave it and its opening clause, not by taking a vote over the words quoted. The clearest cases are r257f2ac, which reports both explicit-to-innocuous substitution and a scatter of the innocuous side across four different categories, and rea44798 and r97dba1f, which report both breadth and explicitness; if multiple membership were permitted, r257f2ac would belong in Wide scatter tight cluster as well, and rea44798 and r97dba1f would belong in Explicit versus sanitized as well. Third, Explicit versus sanitized has ten members and is the obvious candidate for a split. The split I considered and rejected was between descriptions where the unmarked side reconstructs a whole coherent alternative situation (r096d02f, rf69eb30, and to a degree r257f2ac) and descriptions that merely report which vocabulary sits on each side (rb789759, r3f48db3, r7a8495d, r7bd919f). I rejected it because that distinction tracks how expansively each rater chose to narrate what they saw rather than a difference in the relation they identified, and I would not defend it to someone who thought it was one construct.
